The Sharavathi river drops over a cliff in four streams, one of India’s tallest waterfalls. Best seen during and after the monsoon.
A wide, horseshoe-shaped waterfall on the Ghataprabha river, with a pretty hanging bridge nearby.
Twin waterfalls on the Kaveri. A hydroelectric station built here in 1902 was one of Asia’s earliest.
A quiet pilgrim town with an old Shiva temple and calm beaches such as Om, Kudle and Half Moon.
A famous stretch where the highway runs between the Arabian Sea and the Souparnika river.
A small island with striking hexagonal rock columns formed by ancient volcanic activity.
A Shiva temple on a hill by the Arabian Sea, with a very tall gopura and a giant Shiva statue.
A temple town known for its long tradition of feeding every visitor and welcoming pilgrims from all backgrounds.
Home of the Sharada Peetha, a monastery tradition linked to the 8th-century philosopher Adi Shankaracharya.
The Keshava temple, built in the 13th century, is a star-shaped Hoysala temple with richly carved walls.
A hill temple to goddess Chamundeshwari, the patron deity of the Mysuru royal family, with a giant Nandi bull on the way up.
An island fort on the Kaveri and the capital of Tipu Sultan, who died defending it in 1799. The Ranganathaswamy temple is also here.
A huge stone fort built across rocky hills and expanded under the Nayaka rulers, with temples, granaries and water tanks inside.
A 15th-century fort of the Bahmani sultans in the far north, with palaces and an old underground water system called karez nearby.
A hill fortress near Bengaluru that was a summer retreat of Tipu Sultan, famous for sunrise views above the clouds.
The highest peak in Karnataka, in the Baba Budan Giri range where coffee growing in India is said to have begun.
A hill station once used as a summer retreat by the Wodeyar kings, with waterfalls and rose gardens.
A rainforest village known for rain and sunsets, often called the Cherrapunji of the South.
A national park of grassy peaks and shola forest, named for a horse-face-shaped hill.
A tiger reserve and forest park, part of the Nilgiri biosphere, home to elephants, gaur and tigers.
A dense forest reserve beside the Kabini river, well known for elephant herds and wildlife safaris.
